name: social contact
description: There are many sensations created by encounters with other people.

variations.name: friendly contact
variations.description: Being amongst people perceived as accepting important aspects of your identity. Of course, there's a wide range of sensations within this category. e.g. If you haven't seen this friend for a long time, there may be joy or anxiety. Or it could be a stranger who seems warm and open.

variations.name: transactional contact
variations.description: Expecting other people to just do their jobs and not push unnecessary social stress into your day. e.g. The checkout person at the grocery store can exchange general pleasantries, but is not expected to ask you about past medical problems.

variations.name: unfriendly contact
variations.description: A social encounter with a notable element of tension. The could be an outright enemy, or maybe someone who perceived as having wronged you, or someone who makes you nervous about your safety, or someone who appears to fit into a category of those who would not accept an important aspect of your identity.

variations.name: anonymous contact
variations.description: Being amongst others but not explicitly interacting with them. For example, 'people watching' is a kind of social contact even it's just reading body language and cultural signaling.

variations.name: foreign contact
variations.description: Trying to communicate with a person who doesn't share your language. Related to anonymous contact, but you're directly interacting and trying to communicate something. An inability to communicate your intentions could lead to frustration, annoyance, humor, humility, or anything in-between.

variations.name: undesired contact
variations.description: Being in a certain social situation when you'd much rather be somewhere else.

commentaries.quote: We are deeply social creatures with a nuanced ability to perceive the social situation. Unless you're a psychopath, your social sense is as developed and important as your sense of smell.

We can choose what strategy we take when engaging in social contacts of different types: giving others the benefit of the doubt, assuming they're going to cheat us if possible, or just whatever our mood is at the moment.
